config.productsLabel: How many different products this inventory carries
config.maxStackLabel: Maximum quantity of any one item

config.depthWorldNote: These limits come from Merchant’s world settings. This inventory’s Depth setting scales them up or down.

config.drawLabel: How many items to draw from this table

config.noInventories: No inventories yet. Add one to start stocking this merchant.

config.pricingNone: No price until one is agreed with the party on the slate.

config.queryUnavailable: Stocking from the compendiums needs a newer Coffee Pub Blacksmith. Until then this shelf draws from its roll tables.
config.manualNote: Nothing is drawn in. Whatever you put on this shelf is all it carries, and a restock tops those rows back up to their quantity without adding anything you did not choose.
config.addInventoryHint: Add a container to this merchant — a shelf, a back room, a case of curios.

config.portraitTooltip: Click to change the portrait. The token art changes with it.
config.illustrationHint: A picture of the place itself, shown behind the merchant card, and a tint washed over it. Clear either to remove it.
config.tint: Merchant tint — a colour for this merchant’s card

config.removeSourceTooltip: Take this compendium off the list
config.sourceMissingTooltip: This compendium is no longer installed. Nothing is drawn from it.

config.dropTable: Drop a roll table here to stock this inventory by rolling
config.drawNote: Existing items are restocked first. Draws then add new items the merchant doesn’t already carry.
config.soundHint: Leave either as Default and this merchant follows the world setting, so changing that moves every merchant that has not chosen for itself.
config.hideInventoryTooltip: On display — click to put it away
config.showInventoryTooltip: Hidden from players — click to bring it out front
config.fullscreenHint: Which ways in take over the screen. Anyone can still press Full Screen or Leave Full Screen on their own window, and that beats this for that shop.
config.deliveryPhysicalHint: This shop will hold a Ground parcel until somebody comes for it, so it is offered as a place other shops can deliver to.
config.deliveryPortalHint: The Boundless Order Interplanar Network Keep: magic catalogues, clerks who know your face, and a ring in the back room. Members show the BOINK badge on their card, can be sent to and from by Parcel Portal, and are offered as a destination anywhere in the world.
config.deliveryPlacesNote: Places that are not shops — an inn, a guild hall, a name the party made up — are a list for the whole world, in Settings under Merchant → Mail Order. One list serves every shop, so there is nothing to retype here.
config.applyProfileTooltip: Set this shop up as the chosen kind of shop. Nothing already here is removed.
config.profileNote: A profile sets the shop up and adds the shelves it names, with the compendiums, filters and restock cadence a shop like that would use. It never removes a shelf you already have, and it never touches the stock on one.

config.profileKeeps: Shelves already on this merchant are left exactly as they are, stock included.
config.profileFailed: That profile could not be applied.

config.saveProfileNote: Reuse this shop’s setup on other merchants.

config.saveProfileFailed: That profile could not be saved.

settings.soundSlateAddHint: Played when something is put on the slate, to buy or to sell.
settings.soundSlateUpdateHint: Played when a quantity or a price on the slate is changed.
settings.soundSlateClearHint: Played when a line is taken off the slate, or the whole slate is wiped.
settings.soundTransactionHint: Played when goods and coin change hands.
settings.soundRestockHint: Played to the GM when an inventory or a whole merchant finishes restocking.
settings.soundErrorHint: Played when an action is refused or fails.
settings.headingMerchantHint: Merchants and merchants: a token marked as a merchant opens a merchant window players can buy from and sell to. What a merchant stocks, what it charges and when it is open are set on the merchant itself — these are the world-wide rules every merchant plays by.
settings.headingStockDepthHint: Controls how many copies of a single item a merchant can stock at once. Type, rarity, and price each set a limit; the lowest applicable limit wins. An inventory’s Depth setting scales these limits up or down. 0 means no limit.
settings.headingStockByTypeHint: Set stock limits by item type. A merchant might carry ten healing potions, but only one or two of the same weapon.
settings.headingStockByRarityHint: Set stock limits by rarity. Rarer items can be limited even when their type or price would otherwise allow more.
settings.headingSoundHint: What a merchant sounds like. Chosen by the GM for the table, but played only on the client that did the thing — nobody else hears you drop a rope onto your slate. Silent by default.
settings.headingPinsHint: How a merchant pin looks on the map. The icon is not here — it comes from the merchant’s kind, so an apothecary and a weaponsmith are told apart without configuring anything. These apply to pins made from now on; a pin already placed keeps the look it was made with.
settings.headingAestheticsHint: What a merchant looks like in this world: the card a player opens, and the mark on the map. The merchant settings are copied onto a merchant when it becomes one, so changing them later never rewrites a merchant somebody has already dressed.
settings.headingShopLookHint: Defaults for a new merchant. Both are blank on purpose — a world-wide tint would make every merchant the same colour, and a world-wide illustration would put the same tavern behind every counter. Set either and new merchants start there; each merchant can still be changed.
settings.headingAbandonedHint: What a party finds when the merchant behind a merchant is gone but its pin is still on the map. Nobody strips a place completely — whoever left took the stock and the till and left what was not worth carrying.
settings.abandonedStockHint: Item names separated by semicolons — semicolons, because names like “Rope, Hempen (50 feet)” contain commas. Each merchant gets a handful of every one, between one and five; add “x” and a number to fix it: Torch x5. Looked up in your compendiums when the merchant is opened, so renaming a pack never breaks them. Leave it empty for merchants that are stripped bare.
settings.pinTextMaxWidth: Characters per line (0 for one line)
settings.soundWindowOpenHint: Played when a merchant window opens, on the client that opened it. A merchant can choose its own in Merchant Settings.
settings.soundWindowCloseHint: Played when a merchant window closes. A merchant can choose its own in Merchant Settings.
settings.headingMarkersHint: A badge on every merchant token saying what it sells, wearing the category’s own icon in the pin colours above. Without it the only way to learn a token is a shop is to double-click it, which is a poor way to learn that most tokens are not.
